The file path and name to use on the machine the Nuke Server is running on.

Since the machine running Nuke and Unreal Engine might be different, and have different operating systems, we have added support for the TCL getenv command in the Nuke Server, so the Unreal Engine Movie Render Queue will use the correct path from the machine and operating system it is running on to write to. For example, [getenv ENVIRONMENT_VAR] will be resolved to the environment variable set on each operating system.

The use of an environement variable will also allow the UnrealReader to read the written out files from the shared remote location.

A filter that lets you refine the available options in the Map pulldown knob. Searches can contain multiple words separated by the wildcard character '*' (e.g. shot0*take001*v002 will match to cinematics/shot001/take0014/v002)

The list of expressions for selected object names.

Type in object names directly to add their corresponding ID layers to the output. Use commas to create a list of object names to pick in a single line.

Use the wilcard character '*' to select all of the objects matching a given wildcard expression throughout the sequence (e.g. flower* can be used to select objects named flower1, flower2 and flower3).

Escape special characters with '\\' if they appear in an object name (e.g. flower\\* would allow an object named 'flower*' to be selected exactly instead of being resolved as a wildcard expression).

Remove occlusion from stencil layers. When this option is set, actors that occlude the selected actors will be hidden prior to rendering. This will remove reflections of the hidden objects. If not set, the occlusion will be baked into the render.

description.plain_text: UnrealReader: Gives the ability to request and read renders from an open Unreal Engine session. Allows quick and easy reads of render outputs from a frame in any Unreal sequence using any map. Adds control over what settings should be used when rendering such as anti-aliasing, motion blur and camera settings.
